evidence: Layering is clean and directional: lev/engine.py exposes pure functions (tokenize, softmax, raw_choice_scores, blend), lev/loop.py orchestrates them, lev/cli.py only wires argv to classify() — composition of collaborators, no back-and-forth calls.
Dict-to-domain translation happens in exactly one obvious place: question_from_dict in lev/router.py:4-19 is the sole boundary translator from untyped JSON to frozen dataclasses.

Handoffs are explicit and typed: all cross-module contracts flow through frozen dataclasses in lev/types.py (ChoiceQuestion/ScoreQuestion/ChoiceResult/ScoreResult), so inputs/outputs across boundaries are minimal and unsurprising.

Error propagation across the seam is predictable: router and loop raise ValueError for bad input; cli.py:36-38 catches (ValueError, KeyError, OSError) once at the top and converts to exit code 1 — a single, obvious lifecycle boundary.
Minor friction: lev/cli.py:41 serializes results via result.__dict__, an implicit contract on dataclass internals rather than an explicit serialization point.
Minor noise: lev/loop.py:2 imports Counter but never uses it — dead weight at an otherwise clean engine→loop seam.
mid_level_elegance.issues_preventing_higher_score: cli.py:41 relies on result.__dict__ for JSON output, an implicit serialization contract that breaks if result types gain non-serializable fields; and loop.py:2 carries an unused Counter import at the engine/loop boundary.

mid_level_elegance.dimension_character: This tiny codebase has textbook seams: a pure-function engine, a single orchestration loop layer, one boundary translator (question_from_dict), and shared frozen-dataclass contracts, with errors raised deep and handled once at the CLI edge. A new team member can trace any handoff in one hop. The only rough edges are cosmetic: an unused import at the loop seam and result serialization via __dict__ instead of an explicit asdict.
mid_level_elegance.score_rationale: Against the global anchors this sits between 90 (strong, minor friction) and 100 (exemplary): boundaries are explicit, minimal, and unsurprising with translation in one obvious place, but the __dict__ serialization in cli.py and the unused Counter import in loop.py are small, real frictions at otherwise clean seams. Nothing here is recurring glue-code entropy, so the score stays near the top of the scale rather than drifting toward 80.

issues.summary: CLI serializes results via result.__dict__, an implicit boundary contract on dataclass internals
evidence: cli.py:41 does print(json.dumps(result.__dict__, indent=2)) — output shape is derived from dataclass field layout rather than an explicit serialization point, so adding a non-JSON-serializable field (e.g. a Counter or tuple) to ChoiceResult/ScoreResult silently breaks the CLI seam.
issues.suggestion: Use dataclasses.asdict(result) in cli.py:41 to make the serialization point explicit, or add a to_dict() on the result types; single-line change.

issues.summary: Unused Counter import at the engine→loop module seam
evidence: loop.py:2 imports Counter from collections but never references it — dead import noise on a module whose only job is orchestrating engine functions.
issues.suggestion: Delete the unused 'from collections import Counter' line in loop.py:2.
